messages.subject: Re: [breedR] joint use of additive and dominance genomic relationship matrices as generic components
messages.subject_clean: [breedR] joint use of additive and dominance genomic relationship matrices as generic components
messages.body_plain:
Due to the extreme values I reported, here is what is returned by the command cov2cor(fit$reml$invAI):

          geno.add geno.dom Residual
 geno.add        1      NaN      NaN
 geno.dom      NaN        1      NaN
 Residual      NaN      NaN        1

That's interesting: I thought of lack of identifiability, but not for too long, as the A and D matrices aren't too similar. Moreover, I didn't expect such a simple case (genotypes from coalescent + phenotypes from LMM) to be difficult to fit. Finally, INLA (with default priors for generic0 <https://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/doc/latent/generic0.pdf>) works well on the same data set. It would be interesting to see how breedR works when/if Gibbs sampling is added (I can do some beta testing ;).

Le vendredi 30 septembre 2016 17:24:26 UTC+2, ƒacu.- a écrit :
>
> Mmmm, looks very much like lack of identifiability.
>
> Can you check `cov2cor(fit$reml$invAI)` (from the model fiitted with AI) and confirm that the correlation between geno.add and geno.dom is near 1 (or -1)?
>
> If so, you are doing nothing wrong. There is just not enough info in the data to tell apart the dominance and the additive effects.
>
> You would need to go Bayesian and sort out the confusion using sensible priors.
>
> ƒacu.-
>
> El 29/09/2016 a las 15:33, Timothée Flutre escribió:
> > Hello, me again,
> >
> > I learned how to use one generic component <https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/wiki/Overview#generic-component>, but can't succeed in working with two.
> >
> > Here are some details:
> > I simulated genotypes via the coalescent for I individuals.
> > Then, I used the "classical" formulas from Vitezica et al (2013) to estimate the additive and dominance genomic relationship matrices, A and D.
> > Finally, I simulated phenotypes with Q replicates per individual (several years), for a total of N = Q x I observations, according to y = W c + Z a + Z d + e, where y and e are Nx1, c is Qx1 (fixed-effects), a and d are Ix1, with a ~ MVN_I(0, sigma_a^2 A), d ~ MVN_I(0, sigma_d^2 D) and e ~ MVN_N(0, sigma_e^2 Id). i used values sigma_a^2 = 15, sigma_d^2=0 or 3, and sigma_e^2 = 5.
> >
> > I then use breedR like this:
> >
> >
> > fit <- remlf90(fixed=response ~ 1 + year,
> >
> >                generic=list(geno.add=list(model.matrix(~ modelAD$dat$geno - 1), A),
> >
> >                             geno.dom=list(model.matrix(~ modelAD$dat$geno - 1), D))),
> >
> >                data=modelAD$dat,
> >
> >                method="ai")))
> >
> >
> > When I simulate with A only, and fit with A ("ai"), the varcomp estimates are fine: hat{sigma}_a^2 ~= 15 and hat{sigma}_e^2 ~= 5.
> > When I simulate with A and D, and fit with A only ("ai"), the estimate of sigma_a^2 is over-estimated, as expected: hat{sigma}_a^2 ~= 20 and hat{sigma}_e^2 ~= 4.
> > When I simulate with A and D, and fit with A and D ("ai"), all varcomp estimates are completely off: hat{sigma}_a^2 = hat{sigma}_d^2 ~= 1.00e-10 and hat{sigma}_e^2 ~= 1.49e+06
> > When I simulate with A and D, and fit with A and D ("em"), varcomp estimates are not all fine: hat{sigma}_a^2 = hat{sigma}_d^2 ~= 10 and hat{sigma}_e^2 ~= 5.
> >
> > What did I do wrong?
> >
> >
> > ps: A and D are strongly correlated along their diagonal, but the pattern is quite different for their off-diagonal values; moreover, A is singular, but not D
> >
> >

messages.subject: model formulation
messages.body_plain:
Dear breedR users,

I am coming with simple question concerning to model formulation.
Lets consider the example

res.blk <- remlf90(fixed  = phe_X ~ gg,
                   genetic = gen.globulus,
                   spatial = list(model = 'blocks',
                                  coord = globulus[, c('x','y')],
                                  id = 'bl'),
                   data = globulus)

Assuming that there is no genetic group in studied material, what will be the right way to write the model in breedR?

Could I use 1 instead gg?

Jan

messages.subject: Re: [breedR] model formulation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jan!

Yes, you put `1` instead of `gg` to just fit a global mean.

You will also want to define `gen.globulus` appropriately. Do you have a pedigree, or maybe families?

ƒacu.-

messages.subject: UBUNTU Installation
messages.body_plain:
Dear Facundo,

Today I have installed breedR on UBUNTU 16.04.

I had the following problem:

ERROR: failed to lock directory R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.3’ for modifying

I have solved the problem using the following:

install.packages('breedR',dependencies=TRUE, INSTALL_opts = c('--no-lock'))

It works perfectly.

Thanks a lot

Stefano

messages.subject: Re: [breedR] UBUNTU Installation
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for reporting Stefano.

However, I'd say this is circumstantial rather than a general issue.

This 'failed to lock directory' error can arise from time to time when some other package (or previous installation of the same package) didn't finish correctly for some reason, and left the directory locked. If this is the case, it is simply solved by manually removing the .LOCK00 (or something like that) directory within the library directory.

Can you please check whether this is the case and if you can reinstall breedR correctly after removing the .LOCK dir?

Thanks

        ƒacu.-

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
Thank you Facundo.
In some cases we have no information about genetic group, that why it is only family structure. In this case open pollinated (half-sib).

head(pod.df)
  self mum dad x  y Blok Rz Kol Numer_rodu H2015 H2016 Przy Uwagi
1  300  82   0 1 11    1  1   1         82   115   168   53
2  301  54   0 2 11    1  1   2         54   111   158   47
3  302 126   0 3 11    1  1   3        126   116   155   39
4  303  80   0 4 11    1  1   4         80   137   196   59
5  304 188   0 5 11    1  1   5        188   110   178   68
6  305  23   0 6 11    1  1   6         23    80   120   40     D

I defined pedigree
gen.pod <- list(model    = 'add_animal',
                     pedigree = pod.df[,1:3],
                     id       = 'self')

res.blk <- remlf90(fixed  = H2016 ~ 1,
                   genetic = gen.pod,

                   spatial = list(model = 'blocks',

                                  coord = pod.df[, c('x','y')],
                                  id = 'Blok'),
                   data = pod.df)

In that case summarizing res.blk

> summary(res.blk)
Linear Mixed Model with pedigree and spatial effects fit by AI-REMLF90 ver. 1.122
   Data: pod.df
   AIC   BIC logLik

             Estimate    S.E.
Heritability   0.9796 0.01653

Fixed effects:
           value   s.e.
Intercept 145.84 3.0363

I can estimate predicted genetic effects for for all individuals ranef(res.blk). The same is for other spatial models 'splines' and 'AR'

What is your recommendation in order to estimate breeding value for families (in that case  -- mum)?

Best regards,
Jan
